subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals and term/pricing checklist
messages:
From: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@amazonaws.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T16:22:00Z
Subject: Intro: CloudBuyer private offer request

Hi Lauren / Sergio,

Following up from our co-sell sync — CloudBuyer (contact: Maya Singh) is ready to move forward with an AWS Marketplace private offer. High-level ask from the buyer:
- Term: 12 months
- Pricing: they are asking for ~20% off list for committed usage (volume to be negotiated)
- Billing: prefer consolidated billing via AWS (buyer wants charges on AWS invoice) or net-45 vendor invoicing if needed
- Approvals: procurement + finance + legal review required on their side

Can Redwood confirm:
1) whether a 12-month private offer with a 20% discount is doable from a pricing-floor perspective
2) any minimum commitment we want to require for that discount
3) standard doc set procurement usually needs (PO template, SOW, SOC2 statement, marketplace private-offer flow)

I attached a quick worksheet with the initial numbers (RBW-AWS-PrivateOffer-20261110.xlsx). If we can lock pricing and commit levels today, I’ll create the private offer draft in the AWS console and share the link with the buyer so procurement can start their review.

Thanks — appreciate a quick thumbs up or the owners for each item.

Best,
Tom Jenkins
Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
amazonaws.com

Attachment: RBW-AWS-PrivateOffer-20261110.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@amazonaws.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-11T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro: CloudBuyer private offer request

Tom — thanks for the intro and worksheet. Looping in internal owners and outlining a short checklist so we’re aligned with CloudBuyer’s procurement team.

Internal owner assignments (proposed):
- Pricing approval & commitment floor: Sergio Alvarez (cc’d)
- Procurement coordination & AWS console private-offer creation: Lauren Bishop (me)
- Legal redlines and marketplace-term exceptions: Vanessa Ortiz (cc’d)

Checklist for the private offer (what we will provide):
- Finalized price tiers and minimum commit (Sergio to confirm)
- Standard AWS private offer packet: AWS PO instructions, Redwood Master Services Agreement (MSA) excerpt, SOC 2 summary, data handling blurb
- Suggested term language: 12 months with one-time auto-renew opt-out (we recommend 12 months non-auto-renew for first deal unless buyer requests renew)
- Billing: confirm buyer preference for AWS-invoiced charges vs vendor billing — we can support AWS consolidated billing if the buyer uses an AWS account to accept the private offer.

Action items / timing:
- Sergio: confirm target discount floor and minimum commit by EOD (today)
- Lauren: request buyer PO template and procurement timeline (Maya) — I’ll create the private offer draft after pricing is approved
- Vanessa: will prepare a short redline-ready terms doc if buyer legal asks for tweaks

Maya — can you drop your procurement PO template and expected review date? If procurement needs a vendor invoice instead of AWS invoicing, flag that so we can coordinate billing setup.

Thanks — I’ll hold off creating the private offer until Sergio confirms pricing.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: CloudBuyer_PO_Template.pdf (referenced by buyer if provided)
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudbuyer.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procure@cloudbuyer.com
Date: 2026-11-11T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals and term/pricing checklist

Thanks Lauren — quick answers from procurement at CloudBuyer: 
- We are comfortable with a 12-month term.
- Billing: preferred is consolidated AWS invoicing (i.e., charges appear on our AWS invoice via private offer). If that's not possible, we can accept vendor invoicing on net-45 terms.
- Procurement will start formal review on Tuesday (2026-11-16). They need: MSA or exhibit, SOC2 summary, PO template, and the private offer link so the legal team can verify pricing/terms.

I’ve attached our PO template here in case you need it. Also, our CISO may request a short questionnaire about data residency — can your security team provide a one-page summary?

Procurement point of contact: Anita Rao (procure@cloudbuyer.com) — she’ll coordinate signatures.

We want to move quickly; if you can provision the draft private offer and DocuSign link before the review on Tuesday that would be ideal.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Cloud Engineering, CloudBuyer Inc.
Attachment: CloudBuyer_PO_Template.pdf (pdf)
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@amazonaws.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, maya.singh@cloudbuyer.com
Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals and term/pricing checklist

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 15:40 Maya Singh <maya.singh@cloudbuyer.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lauren — quick answers from procurement at CloudBuyer:
> - We are comfortable with a 12-month term.
> - Billing: preferred is consolidated AWS invoicing (i.e., charges appear on our AWS invoice via private offer).

Thanks all — pricing/commit update from our side: after reviewing the worksheet and expected usage profile, pricing is approved at an 18% discount off list for a 12-month private offer with a minimum committed spend of $120,000 over the term. Key notes:
- Discount floor: 18% approved (requires minimum $120k commit)
- Term: 12 months, non-auto-renew (buyer can request renewal at term end)
- Billing: we can enable AWS consolidated billing for the private offer — Lauren, please confirm account-to-account link details when you create the offer
- Legal: Vanessa will produce a short exhibit (2 pages) for the AWS private offer to cover data handling and payment terms

Action items (owner / due):
- Sergio: add pricing tiers to the worksheet and upload final RBW-AWS-PrivateOffer-20261112.xlsx (today)
- Lauren: create private offer draft in AWS console, include DocuSign link for MSA exhibit, and share link with Maya / procurement (due: 2026-11-12 EOD)
- Vanessa: prepare exhibit and redline doc (attachment) for buyer legal review (due: 2026-11-13)
- Maya / Procure: confirm PO issuance timeline (expected next week)

Attaching final redline for internal review: signed-terms-redline.docx (draft). I’ll update the HubSpot deal and add the private-offer ID once the console flow is complete: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-6439

Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Attachment: signed-terms-redline.docx (word)
